meta.title: Portolan — Cloud-native spatial data infrastructure
meta.description: Portolan publishes geospatial data as plain files on object storage. No servers, no databases, no proprietary licenses. Structured metadata lets people and AI agents read a catalog and query it directly.

hero.title: The future of spatial data
hero.description: Portolan publishes geospatial data as plain files on object storage, with no servers, no databases, and no proprietary licenses. Structured metadata lets people and AI agents read a catalog, understand it, and query it directly.

why.title: The job of an SDI has changed.
why.subtitle: Spatial data infrastructure matters more than ever. The architecture underneath it has not kept up.

open.title: Open
open.description: Every format is open and every tool is Apache-2.0. DuckDB, BigQuery, and desktop GIS read the same bytes. If Portolan disappeared tomorrow, your data would still work everywhere.

aiFirst.title: AI-ready
aiFirst.description: An agent can read the catalog and answer questions against it. Plain text files explain how to reach the data, and structured metadata explains what it means. The <link>Finland.SDI demo</link> shows this working against a national SDI.

easy.title: Files in a bucket
easy.description: A traditional SDI needs databases, services, and specialist staff. A Portolan node is files in a bucket. Point the CLI at your data, convert, and push.

scalable.title: Scales with storage
scalable.description: Cloud storage absorbs the load, including agent-scale crawling. There are no servers to size and no capacity to plan. Scaling falls to the most proven layer any cloud offers.

lowCost.title: Two line items
lowCost.description: The whole budget is storage plus egress. Sharing public data should not take an operations team, and a popular dataset should not blow a budget. The <link>cost calculator</link> shows what your data would run.

sovereign.title: Sovereign
sovereign.description: The full stack can live inside your own jurisdiction. Host on AWS, GCS, Azure, MinIO, Hetzner, Scaleway, or any S3-compatible storage. No foreign vendor sits between your agency and its data.

howItWorks.title: Point, convert, push.
howItWorks.subtitle: A shared set of open formats replaces the server. Cloud storage does the scaling. Browsers, query engines, and AI agents read the files directly.

convert.title: Convert
convert.description: Convert shapefiles, GeoTIFFs, WFS, GeoPackage, and ArcGIS Feature Services into cloud-native formats. Vectors become GeoParquet, rasters become COG, and map tiles become PMTiles.

catalog.title: Catalog
catalog.description: Generate a STAC-based catalog that describes every asset with structured metadata. Any STAC tool can read it.

publish.title: Publish
publish.description: Push the files to any S3-compatible object storage. That includes AWS, GCS, Azure, R2, MinIO, and Source Cooperative for free open data hosting.

browse.title: Browse
browse.description: Open the catalog in the Portolan browser or any STAC viewer, query it with DuckDB, or point an agent at the URL. The data answers questions directly.

ecosystem.title: All of it is on GitHub.
ecosystem.subtitle: Six Portolan projects, all Apache-2.0. The formats they publish are community standards, so the wider toolbox already exists.

quickstart.title: Publish your first catalog.
quickstart.intro: Start by browsing a live catalog. Then publish your own with the CLI or with an agent.

browse.title: Browse a catalog
browse.description: Portolan catalogs are live on the web. Open the browser to explore published datasets, or point DuckDB at any GeoParquet URL and query it in place.

cli.title: With the CLI
cli.description: Install portolan-cli, then init, add, check, and push. The CLI converts your files and generates the catalog.

claude.title: With Claude
claude.description: Install the Portolan skill in Claude Code and point it at your data. It handles conversion, metadata, and publishing. Agents excel at CLIs and text files, so non-experts can publish too.

registry.title: Browse {count} catalogs
registry.description: Catalogs published around the world, live in the registry.

cta.title: Have a catalog to share?
cta.description: Submit your Portolan catalog to the registry.

submit.title: Submit a catalog
submit.successDescription: Your catalog will appear after review.

resources.title: Two talks that make the case.
resources.subtitle: Portolan is early-stage and developed in the open. The demos, the cost calculator, and the example catalogs are linked from inside the talks.

holmesTalk.title: A Cloud-Native Geo Upgrade for Spatial Data Infrastructure
holmesTalk.description: Five requirements for a modern SDI, the cloud-native formats that meet them, and a live serverless portal for the Netherlands.

nextSdi.title: The Next SDI
nextSdi.attribution: Javier de la Torre · OGC Connect Helsinki
nextSdi.quote: “SDIs were built for experts; now they must serve agents.”
nextSdi.description: Why de-intermediation makes SDIs more important than ever, and the architecture they need. The live Finland.SDI agent demo closes the talk.
